IPO · CHIRAL AMPLIFICATION MODEL

How does one hand amplify itself?

TEACHING MODEL
R0, S0, [A]→Autocatalysis→ee + rotation
RATESvR = kR[A]Rm, vS = kS[A]Sm; m > 1
BALANCEee = (R−S)/(R+S) × 100%
ROTATIONαobs = [α]ℓc · (ee/100%)
OUTPUTsign(αobs) → dominant enantiomer

R, S mirror products · m nonlinear order
ℓ path length · c concentration · [α] specific rotation

Simplified kinetic lens; real asymmetric autocatalysis can involve multiple species and steps.

WHY IT MATTERS

Small imbalance, amplified

Mirror-image molecules can behave differently in living systems. Their work showed how asymmetric reactions and autocatalysis can strongly amplify a tiny initial preference for one molecular handedness.

Verified source ↗
INPUTA minute chiral imbalance
PROCESSAsymmetric catalysis + self-amplification
OUTPUTPredominantly one molecular handedness
